subject: Energy
title: Fast Breeder Reactors
description: A 60-second lesson on Fast Breeder Reactors.

hook.text: Breeder reactors create more fuel than they consume—converting non-fissile U-238 into fissile plutonium-239.

buildup.text: Fast neutrons (without a moderator) are key—they drive the conversion of U-238 to Pu-239 efficiently.

discovery.text: In theory, breeders could extend uranium supplies by 60 times—using the 99.3% of uranium that normal reactors waste.

twist.text: Sodium-cooled breeders are technically complex—liquid sodium reacts violently with water and burns in air.

climax.text: Few breeders operate today—high costs and proliferation risks (plutonium is bomb material) have slowed development.

punchline.text: Make fuel as you burn it—brilliant in theory, tricky in practice.

quiz.question: What does a breeder reactor produce?
options: More fissile fuel than it consumes
